title: Evaluating Reading Comprehension Exercises Generated by LLMs: A Showcase of ChatGPT in Education Applications
venue: Proceedings of the 18th Workshop on Innovative Use of NLP for Building Educational Applications (BEA 2023)
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of creating high-quality, personalized English reading comprehension materials for middle school students, a task that is labor-intensive for teachers and difficult to scale with traditional content development. The authors investigate whether ChatGPT can be used to generate reading passages and multiple-choice exercise questions that are suitable for classroom use, and whether such outputs compare favorably with human-written materials and a fine-tuned GPT-2 + PPLM baseline.

The intervention is a reading exercise generation system built around ChatGPT. In a zero-shot setting, the system uses crafted prompts to generate passages based on desired topic, length, genre, and CEFR level; in a one-shot setting, it additionally conditions generation on a reference passage. The system also generates multiple-choice questions, answer options, and explanations, with an added toxicity check before content is released. A graphical interface was built for teachers and students to use directly, and the generated content remained editable by teachers.

The study was conducted in the context of Chinese middle schools, using materials collected from Beijing municipal education authorities and eight local middle schools. Evaluation combined automatic metrics, human ratings by Chinese college students and native English speakers, and first-hand feedback from three experienced middle school teachers in Beijing after a week of use. The main conclusion is that ChatGPT-generated passages were rated as highly coherent, readable, suitable, and often better than human-written passages, while generated multiple-choice questions were relevant but weaker in distractor quality and overall pedagogical usefulness. Teachers reported that the system was easy to use and promising for reducing workload while supporting more diverse and personalized learning materials.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s ChatGPT is a conversational large language model chatbot used for generating and adapting text from prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper used ChatGPT to generate middle school English reading comprehension passages and multiple-choice exercise questions in zero-shot and one-shot settings, with prompt-based control over length, genre, difficulty, topic, question count, options, and question type.

findings.finding_summary: Human evaluations found ChatGPT-generated reading passages to be higher quality than both human-written passages and a fine-tuned GPT-2 + PPLM baseline on several dimensions. In Table 2, experienced Chinese student raters gave ChatGPT higher scores than human-written passages for readability (4.61 vs 4.52), correctness (4.60 vs 4.32), coherence (4.65 vs 4.39), engagement (4.37 vs 4.07), and overall quality (4.46 vs 4.18); native speakers also rated ChatGPT highest overall quality (4.06 vs 3.89 human).
findings.measure: Human-rated reading passage quality (readability, correctness, coherence, engagement, overall quality)
findings.sample_size: n=9 Chinese college students; n=364 native English speakers; 30 passages in Example Set 1

findings.finding_summary: In pairwise comparisons, ChatGPT passages were preferred over human-written passages and strongly outperformed the GPT-2 + PPLM baseline. Table 3 shows human-written vs generated preference scores of 0.13 vs 0.87 for ChatGPT zero-shot and 0.20 vs 0.80 for ChatGPT one-shot; Table 4 also showed ChatGPT passages were less likely to be judged model-generated than human-written passages in the comparison setting (e.g., 0.30 generated-likeness for ChatGPT zero-shot vs 0.57 for the baseline).
findings.measure: Pairwise relative quality, perceived model-generatedness, topic coherence, suitability
findings.sample_size: n=9 Chinese college students; 10 human-written passages paired with 30 generated passages

findings.finding_summary: For topic coherence, ChatGPT followed prompt constraints very well. Table 5 reports a topic coherence score of 0.97 for ChatGPT in both zero-shot and one-shot settings, compared with 0.40 for GPT-2 + PPLM on the generated side and 0.87/0.77 on the human side in the comparison framework.
findings.measure: Topic coherence / consistency with given topics
findings.sample_size: n=9 Chinese college students; 10 topic-matched comparisons

findings.finding_summary: The paper also found ChatGPT-generated passages suitable for middle school English learners. Table 6 reports suitability scores of 0.77 for both ChatGPT zero-shot and one-shot, compared with 0.37 for GPT-2 + PPLM; the authors conclude the materials were largely suitable for classroom use.
findings.measure: Suitability for middle school English reading comprehension

findings.finding_summary: For exercise question generation, ChatGPT produced highly relevant but not always optimal multiple-choice questions. Table 7 shows generated questions scored 4.38/5 on match to passage content, but were lower than human-written questions on usefulness (3.25 vs 3.93) and suitability (3.48 vs 3.92), while being more recognizable as model-generated (0.67 vs 0.27).
findings.measure: Human-rated exercise question quality (match, usefulness, suitability, perceived generatedness)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a single empirical system-evaluation study with substantial human evaluation but no randomized intervention or causal educational outcome study. Evidence quality is therefore moderate/qualitative rather than high causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are generally positive and several are large in practical terms, especially for passage quality and prompt adherence. However, the paper does not report standardized effect sizes, so impact is judged as modest-to-strong but not precisely quantified.
